item.title: Most overrated and underrated teams in Week 9 US LBM Coaches Poll
item.description: The latest US LBM Coaches Poll saw some noticeable changes following some dramatic results in Week 9 . This all helps to set the stage for the College Football Playoff selection committee's first batch of playoff rankings this week as the regular season makes the final turn down the final stretch. While we now seem to know which teams are safely in the top 12 (like Miami and Georgia), we also don't really know who else could be viable down toward the bottom of those 12 spots. Chances are a lot of two-loss teams will either be on the right side of the cut or on the outside looking in. Here are the most overrated and underrated teams in this week's coaches poll. Overrated: No. 3 Indiana When you need a miracle 60-yard kick to send a game to overtime against an unranked team, you know you're in trouble. This is the second straight week where Indiana had to struggle through a mistake-filled game, especially considering what is potentially happening in their QB room. With doubts surrounding the status of Josh Hoover, it could be backup Grant Wilson who has to take the wheel the rest of the way. Their next game against a resurgent USC could be a true test of whether this team can truly weather whatever storm is brewing in Bloomington. It's been quite some time since we've seen the Hoosiers struggle. Underrated: No. 4 Utah As of right now, Utah is only one of three unbeaten teams in the sport. And yet, they still aren't considered a top 3 team in the nation. In a potential trap game against a Cincinnati team coming off a win against Texas Tech, they took care of business, trouncing the Bearcats 49-25. Devon Damiper was excellent, throwing for 260 yards and 3 touchdowns, and the run game had over 200 yards on just 42 carries. The Utes now have two of the best wins in the entire conference. Next week? A date with BYU in the Holy War to potentially determine who represents the conference not only in the championship game, but in the CFP as well. Overrated: No. 21 Boise State As the current frontrunner for the Group of Six's lone playoff spot, the Broncos must manuever through what could turn out to be a problematic injury to QB Maddux Madsen. He left their game against Texas State with a left knee injury. True freshman Mat Cutforth had three touchdown passes, but the game was too close for comfort. Boise State can rely on having the nation's rushing leader, but they may not be able to rely on Cutforth for a prolonged period of time should Madsen be sidelined. The Group of Six CFP race just got very interesting. Underrated: No. 15 LSU If you're wondering how an idle team can be underrated, it's about who they play after their bye that should tell you. LSU may be the team that decides the entire fate of the SEC. Next week, they play Alabama at home, then host Texas. Should the Tigers go 2-0, they could become the two-loss team no one wants to face. item.title: Antonelli heads list of F1's youngest champions
item.description: Kimi Antonelli has made history by becoming the youngest title winner in the 77th year of the Formula 1 World Championship. The Italian, at 20 years and 68 days, has beaten the record of Sebastian Vettel, who was 23 years and 133 days old when he won the first of his four drivers' championships in 2010. Antonelli, who was still a teenager until 25 August, has secured the title in his second season in the sport. We take a look at F1's other young champions and how Antonelli's achievement compares with theirs. Kimi Antonelli First championship: 2026 Age: 20 years and 68 days Stage of his F1 career when title was won: Second full season F1 debut: 2025 Australian Grand Prix (aged 18) Antonelli has already broken a number of records on the way to becoming F1's youngest champion. In his second season, he became the youngest driver to achieve a pole position in China and the youngest to lead the championship at the next race in Japan. In Monaco, he became the youngest driver to complete a 'grand slam' of pole position, fastest lap, leading every lap and winning the race. All this after a rookie season in 2025 in which there were occasional highs but plenty of errors, and his final total of 150 points was less than half of the 319 accumulated by Mercedes team-mate George Russell. Sebastian Vettel Sebastian Vettel's four drivers' championships were won between 2010-13 [Getty Images] First championship: 2010 Age: 23 years and 133 days Stage of his F1 career when title was won: Third full season F1 debut: 2007 US Grand Prix (aged 19) Vettel was one of four drivers who could win the title going into the season-ending 2010 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix. He was far from the best placed, though, trailing Ferrari's Fernando Alonso by 15 points before the race and his Red Bull team-mate Mark Webber by seven. The German did what he had to do by winning the grand prix and Alonso could only finish seventh, having become stuck behind the Renault of Vitaly Petrov. With Webber in eighth, Vettel won the championship by four points from Alonso. It was yet another F1 record for Vettel. He had become the youngest F1 points scorer on his debut for BMW Sauber in Indianapolis in 2007, before becoming the then youngest pole sitter and race winner at the 2008 Italian Grand Prix for Toro Rosso. Lewis Hamilton Lewis Hamilton won the 2008 championship by overtaking Timo Glock into the final corner of the Brazilian Grand Prix [Getty Images] First championship: 2008 Age: 23 years and 300 days Stage of his F1 career when title was won: Second full season F1 debut: 2007 Australian Grand Prix (aged 22) Lewis Hamilton's debut season in 2007 almost delivered a fairytale title but he faltered in the final two races of the year. He failed to score in China and finished seventh in Brazil, which allowed Ferrari's Kimi Raikkonen to pip both Hamilton and fellow McLaren driver Fernando Alonso by a single point. item.title: When will the Golden State Valkyries parade be? Here's what to know
item.description: After Golden State Valkyries achieved an historic win, beating the Atlanta Dream, 68-63, Saturday night at Ballhalla, the team announced details of their championship parade! Fans can begin lining up along the parade route at 9 a.m. on the bay side of the Embarcadero. The parade will start at noon and expected to end at 2 p.m. Where will the parade be? Viewers can watch coverage on TV on ABC7, or stream on the free ABC7 Bay Area streaming and mobile app starting at 9:30 a.m. on Wednesday. Who will be there? The team, coaches, staff and city leaders will all be there to celebrate the historic win. item.title: F1 Mexico GP: Kimi Antonelli clinches world title as Max Verstappen holds off Lewis Hamilton for victory
item.description: Motorsport photo Kimi Antonelli has written history by becoming Formula 1's youngest-ever world champion at the Mexico Grand Prix, as Red Bull's Max Verstappen beat Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton to win the race. Verstappen seized control of the race during the only pitstop of the race on lap 28 of 71, leapfrogging early leader Charles Leclerc , and he fended off Leclerc's team-mate Hamilton to take victory, with Antonelli celebrating his maiden F1 title with a podium spot in third. With neither Russell nor Hamilton winning the race, Antonelli's race result was irrelevant, but he underlined his mature title winning campaign with a controlled drive as he picked off Leclerc in the second half of the race. At the start, polesitter Hamilton was challenged by Leclerc for the lead into Turn 2 and again towards Turn 4-5. Leclerc cut the grass to pass his team-mate as Hamilton lost momentum to third-placed Verstappen as well, who took advantage of the intra-team tussle to snatch second away from Hamilton. "I got pushed off by my own team-mate," Hamilton rued, as Verstappen was also angling for Leclerc to hand back the position. The Monegasque only received a five-second penalty for leaving the track and gaining an advantage, which was deemed rather soft by both Verstappen and his own team-mate: "He's got clean air, he doesn't have to manage like the rest of us," Hamilton pointed out. In the background, the second Red Bull of Isack Hadjar was punted off by slow-starting George Russell , who had dropped from second to sixth and was handed a 10-second time penalty. Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing To Hamilton's point, Leclerc soon pulled out a five-second gap to second-placed Verstappen - the Dutchman only frontrunner to start on medium tyres instead of softs. Hamilton trailed by another couple of seconds ahead of the two Mercedes and the two McLaren cars. A strong start from Oscar Piastri saw him move up from a disappointing 12th grid slot to seventh, seven seconds behind the leading train. Leclerc and Verstappen both pitted on lap 28 for their only pitstop, with Leclerc moving to mediums and Verstappen switching to softs. Helped by Leclerc's additional five-second hold, Verstappen was able to jump the Ferrari in pitlane to take charge of the race, albeit on the more brittle tyre compound. "We basically need one of your magic Mexico stints," declared Verstappen's race engineer Gianpiero Lambiase, as Hamilton's next-lap response by collecting mediums dropped the leading trio to fourth, fifth and sixth respectively. It handed Antonelli a brief spell in clear air at the front from Russell and Lando Norris , with Mercedes not having any real strategic options to challenge for the win - not that Antonelli would have minded one bit while on title course. item.title: ‘Firing That Was Long Overdue,’ ‘Right Move for Everyone’ — CFB World Reacts to Mike Norvell’s Departure From Florida State After Clemson Loss
item.description: CFB World Reacts to Mike Norvell’s Departure From Florida State After Clemson Loss. Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Florida State is looking for a new head football coach, and several college football voices who weighed in Sunday backed its decision to move on from Mike Norvell. FSU President Richard McCullough told Norvell that afternoon that the school was changing the program’s leadership, effective immediately. This move came a day after a 36-24 home loss to Clemson dropped the Seminoles to 3-5. Rick Stockstill, an assistant on the staff and a member of the FSU Athletics Hall of Fame, was named interim head coach while the school begins a national search. The Home Loss to Clemson That Preceded Mike Norvell’s Firing Norvell’s seven-year tenure ends with a 41-39 record. Florida State went into Saturday’s game at Doak Campbell Stadium as a 5-point favorite and gave the ball away four times. Quarterback Ashton Daniels threw three interceptions and lost a fumble, and two of those picks set up 10 Clemson points in the second quarter. The Tigers stretched their lead to 29-10 before the Seminoles pulled within 29-24 on Daniels’ 41-yard touchdown pass to Jasen Lopez with 5:30 left. Clemson quarterback Tait Reynolds answered with a 79-yard touchdown run, and FSU’s last drive ended in another interception. item.title: Steelers ‘right where we want to be’ entering bye week
item.description: Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images | Getty Images Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers remained somewhat terse in his postgame press conference following Pittsburgh’s 27-6 win over the Browns on Sunday. Despite the big win over a divisional foe, Rodgers seemed reluctant to give too much praise to the Steelers offense, saying their performance was “not very complete” and that there “should’ve been a lot more points.” Still, with the Steelers now 6-2 on the season, in sole possession of first place in the AFC North, and entering a midseason bye week on a four-game winning streak, Rodgers acknowledged the team is in a good spot. “We’d like to play our best and still win. We also like to win,” he said. “We’re 6-2 going into the bye, first in the division. We’re right where we want to be.” Both Cleveland and Pittsburgh were 5-2 entering Week 8, with the Browns having already defeated the Steelers earlier in the season in a Thursday Night Football matchup at Huntington Bank Field. But back at home in Acrisure Stadium in Sunday’s rematch, the Steelers ran for 200 yards on Cleveland while only allowing 34 yards on the ground en route to a lopsided, 21-point victory. Despite the AFC North being arguably the NFL’s most competitive division in 2026 with not one team under .500, the Steelers are in the best spot of the group at midseason. The now 5-3 Browns lost in blowout fashion. The Bengals (now 5-2) won on Sunday to jump into second place in the division, but it took overtime to defeat the hapless 1-7 Titans. And the Ravens, the consensus preseason pick to win the AFC North, are now in last place at 4-4 after a 36-10 loss to the Buffalo Bills on Sunday. To make matters worse for Baltimore, Lamar Jackson was injured again and is now headed to IR with an upcoming thumb injury. The Steelers’ first game after the bye will be a Sunday Night Football matchup on Nov. 15 against the Bengals in what will be another matchup between top AFC North teams. “Winning is the most important thing — 2-1 in the division now,” Rodgers said. “Either way, that game in two weeks is going to be really important.” The Steelers defeated the Bengals 30-27 earlier in the season. The black and gold have split their series with the Browns in 2026 but still have both matchups against the Ravens due later in the season. While the Steelers players acknowledged there’s a lot of football left to play, T.J. Watt said he’s been encouraged by how the team has found ways to win thus far. “I like that we’ve won games many different ways. We’ve come from behind. We’ve been able to hold leads. item.title: Arizona football still ranked in AP Top 25 after loss to Texas Tech
item.description: LUBBOCK, TEXAS - OCTOBER 31: Kedrick Reescano #3 of the Arizona Wildcats celebrates after scoring a touchdown during the first half of the game against the Texas Tech Red Raiders at Galaxy Stadium on October 31, 2026 in Lubbock, Texas. (Photo by John E. Moore III/Getty Images) | Getty Images Arizona’s loss to Texas Tech on Saturday wasn’t enough to dislodge the Wildcats from the national rankings. Arizona (6-2) is ranked No. 24 in this week’s AP Top 25, down two spots from last week. The UA received 154 points, which is a big drop from a week ago but still 60 points higher than the No. 25-ranked Florida Gators. Arizona is ranked for the third consecutive week in-season for the first time since 2023. Utah is the highest-ranked Big 12 team at No. 3 in the poll. If the Utes defeat No. 7 BYU this Saturday, they’ll come to Tucson the following Saturday with at minimum a top-three ranking. Utah could potentially move a spot or two up the rankings if it wins and Georgia loses to Ole Miss (or voters elevate Utah above a one-loss Bulldogs) or if Miami loses at Notre Dame. Interestingly, Texas Tech didn’t move up the rankings after beating the Wildcats. The Red Raiders are No. 13 in the country. Houston, which is tied with Arizona in the Big 12 standings, moved up one spot to No. 17. The USA Today Coaches poll has Arizona ranked No. 22. Arizona faces TCU on Friday night at 8:15 p.m. MST.

item.description: Italian formula One driver Kimi Antonelli of team Mercedes drives during the Mexican Grand Prix at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez. He is also the first Italian to be crowned world champion since Alberto Ascari in 1953. Antonelli sealed the title after finishing third at the Mexican Grand Prix. With four races to go, his closest challengers - team-mate George Russell and Lewis Hamilton of Ferrari - cannot catch him in the standings. Max Verstappen of Red Bull won the race in Mexico.

Antonelli secured the final spot on the podium at the Mexican Grand Prix , finishing third behind race winner Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton. The Italian delivered a composed performance despite the numerous interruptions and Safety Car periods, maintaining his position in the closing stages to secure the result he needed to become Formula 1 world champion. Antonelli is only in his second season in Formula 1 this year. The Mercedes driver is just 20 years and 68 days old at the moment he clinches the title. item.description: Andrea Kimi Antonelli is the 2026 F1 world champion after the Mexico GP, becoming the youngest title winner ever at 20 years, 68 days in only his second season. Mercedes ’ Antonelli had his first shot at the title in Austin and sealed it in this weekend’s F1 Mexico GP by finishing third. He arrived in Mexico with 365 points, 123 clear of teammate George Russell and 124 clear of Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton, who both had only an outside chance. It has been a dominant season, with Antonelli adjusting well to the new car and regulations. Going into Mexico, he had 9 wins from 18 Grands Prix, 15 podiums and 7 poles, including five wins in a row from China to Monaco. Russell started well by winning the season opener, but three retirements hurt his challenge. Antonelli is now the 36th driver to be crowned Formula 1 champion, and only the third from Italy after Giuseppe Farina and Alberto Ascari. The country waited 73 years for another one. GRANDE KIMI!! YOU ARE THE F1 WORLD CHAMPION!! https://t.co/OO6kmAM3LY — Mercedes-AMG PETRONAS F1 Team (@MercedesAMGF1) November 1, 2026 Antonelli and Mercedes by the Numbers Youngest F1 World Champion: Andrea Kimi Antonelli at 20 years, 68 days (2026), beating Sebastian Vettel’s 23 years, 134 days (2010) by 1,162 days, and Lewis Hamilton’s 23 years, 300 days (2008). Number of F1 World Champions: 36 (Antonelli is the 36th driver to win a drivers’ championship). F1 World Champions From Italy: Giuseppe Farina (1950), Alberto Ascari (1952 and 1953) and Andrea Kimi Antonelli (2026). Most Wins by an Italian in One Season: Antonelli (9 in 2026), beating Ascari’s 6 (1952). Most Career Wins by an Italian: Ascari (13), then Antonelli (9) and Riccardo Patrese (6). Most Career Poles by an Italian: Ascari (14), Patrese (8) and Antonelli (7). Youngest F1 Pole-Sitter: Antonelli, who took the record from Vettel in China this season. (Photo by Clive Rose/Getty Images) Youngest F1 Race Winners: Antonelli is second on the list , behind Max Verstappen. His China win also made him the first Italian to win a Grand Prix since Giancarlo Fisichella in Malaysia in 2006, RACER reported . Italian GP: Antonelli won at Monza from 19th on the grid , becoming the first Italian to win the race since Ludovico Scarfiotti in 1966. Drivers to Win the F1 Championship With Mercedes: Juan Manuel Fangio (1954 and 1955), Lewis Hamilton (2014, 2015, 2017, 2018, 2019 and 2020), Nico Rosberg (2016) and Andrea Kimi Antonelli (2026). It is the team’s 10th drivers’ title and its first since 2020. Antonelli, lad with a ruthless cutting edge intertwined with a feverishly boyish charm, gestured and laughed with his team down below. While it was a comical blunder, comparisons to his namesake Finnish driver (sadly for this section, Antonelli’s middle name was not in tribute to Raikkonen) seem somewhat appropriate for the 20-year-old Italian who, on Sunday night, became the youngest Formula 1 world champion ever. Raikkonen, Ferrari ’s last champion in 2007, was known as “The Iceman”, such was his cold, unflustered demeanour. And in just his second F1 season, Antonelli’s poise and serenity have been his biggest asset amid the season of his life. Antonelli’s third-place finish in Mexico, off the back of his brilliant lights-to-flag victory in Austin last week, rather epitomised the Italian’s near-flawless campaign – and that of his forlorn Mercedes teammate, George Russell . While Antonelli made ground at the start in Mexico City, Russell dropped back and received a 10-second penalty after spinning Isack Hadjar. It rather summed up the forlorn Briton’s year. Antonelli has not just beaten teammate George Russell this season but wiped the floor with him this year (Getty) A season which had Russell as the clear pre-season favourite – in the quickest car on the grid – has resulted in Toto Wolff ’s Italian protege, the teen he trusted with filling Lewis Hamilton ’s seismic boots, dominating the 2026 campaign. And for Antonelli, it is a history-making achievement. At 20 years and 68 days, the Italian becomes the sport’s youngest-ever champion in its 76-year history, beating Sebastian Vettel’s previous record at 23 years of age. In quite the twist of fate, Antonelli was actually born on the same day that Vettel made his F1 race weekend debut in Turkey in August 2006. Astonishingly, Antonelli also becomes Italy’s first world champion in 73 years, when the great Alberto Ascari won for Ferrari in 1963. Alongside multiple Grand Slam champion Jannik Sinner, he is now Italian sport’s biggest star.
